beats: Hook: the GPU finishes its work faster than the CPU can tell it what to do next. [line_cg_relay_baton, line_cg_conductor_sheets]
Eager mode: every small operation is its own kernel launched by the CPU; the GPU timeline is mostly gaps. [line_cg_conductor_sheets, line_tired_dog_street, line_clock_face, line_gpu]
torch.compile fuses the small kernels into fewer, bigger ones (a one-line change): fewer trips. [line_cg_one_trip, line_glue_tiles]
mode="reduce-overhead": record the whole launch sequence once as a CUDA graph and replay it with one launch (the player piano roll). [line_cg_punch_roll, line_cg_player_piano, line_clockwork]
Graph breaks make several graphs, each with its own memory; CUDA Graph Trees let them share one memory pool. [line_cg_roll_boxes, line_slip_boxes]

Unsafe operations (a CPU sync such as .cpu()) cannot be recorded; Inductor graph partition cuts the graph around them, records the pieces and runs the unsafe part live. [line_cg_roll_scissors, line_cg_live_handplay, line_scissors_strips]
In vLLM: tag the custom op as cudagraph-unsafe, optionally register a wrapper; PT2 splits and wraps each partition. [line_cg_bell_tag, line_ticket, line_spike]
Takeaway: when the kernels are tiny the launches are the cost; record once, replay many times. [line_cg_player_piano, line_dog_chases_cat]
Cover (line_cover_l11_02; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the player piano plays its recorded roll by itself while the conductor rests in an armchair.
